problems.title: Sign of a logarithmic fraction
problems.question: Solve $\log_{0.5}(x^2+3)/(4x^2-16x)<0$.
problems.idea: The numerator is always negative, so the denominator must be positive.
steps: x²+3≥3>1 for every real x, so the logarithm exists and is strictly negative.
A negative numerator gives a negative fraction exactly when x(x-4)>0.
This holds for x<0 or x>4. Both poles are excluded.

problems.title: Infer a logarithm’s monotonicity from one input
problems.question: logₐ(x²-11x+30)>logₐ(14-x) is known to hold at x=1. Solve it.
problems.idea: The known input tells us whether the base is above or below one.
formulas: For a>1, logarithms preserve order; for 0<a<1, they reverse it.
steps: At x=1 the arguments are 20 and 13. Since logₐ20>logₐ13, the base must satisfy a>1.
The domain is (x-5)(x-6)>0 and x<14, giving x<5 or 6<x<14.
Compare arguments: x²-11x+30>14-x gives (x-2)(x-8)>0, hence x<2 or x>8.
Intersect with the domain to get x<2 or 8<x<14.

problems.title: Domain of a square root containing logarithms
problems.question: Find the domain of $y=\sqrt{-8(\log_9x)^2+\log_{1/3}x+3}$.
problems.idea: Use a single logarithm variable and require a nonnegative radicand.
formulas: A real square root needs its radicand ≥0.
steps: First x>0. Put t=log₉x.
The radicand condition is -8t²-2t+3≥0, or (4t+3)(2t-1)≤0.
The base 9 exceeds one, so 9^(-3/4)≤x≤9^(1/2).

problems.title: Volume of a hexagonal pyramid from edge inclination
problems.question: A regular hexagonal pyramid has lateral edge 1, making 60° with its base. Find the volume.
problems.idea: Resolve the edge into a height and a base circumradius.
formulas: For a regular hexagon, side=R and base area=3√3R²/2.
steps: The base area is (3√3/2)(1/4)=3√3/8.

problems.title: Multiply logarithms with opposite signs
problems.question: Solve log₃0.7·log₁/₃(x-6)<0.
problems.idea: Determine the constant factor’s sign first.
formulas: For base above one, the logarithm of a number in (0,1) is negative.
For base in (0,1), log_b t>0 iff 0<t<1.
steps: log₃0.7<0, so the other factor must be positive.
Thus 0<x-6<1, which also enforces the logarithm domain.
Adding 6 gives 6<x<7.

problems.title: Simplify reciprocal nested logarithms
problems.question: Solve $\log_3\log_4\frac{4x-1}{x+1}-\log_{1/3}\log_{1/4}\frac{x+1}{4x-1}<0$.
problems.idea: Both inner logarithms are equal; the outer bases are reciprocal.
steps: Put u=(4x-1)/(x+1), t=log₄u. Both outer logarithms require t>0.
The inequality is 2log₃t<0, hence 0<t<1.
This means 1<u<4. Write u=4-5/(x+1). The upper bound requires x>-1.
On x>-1, the lower bound u>1 gives 3x>2. Thus x>2/3, which satisfies every denominator and logarithm restriction.

problems.title: A nested logarithm gives a rational sign chart
problems.question: Solve $\log_{0.5}\log_8\frac{x^2-2x}{x-3}<0$.
problems.idea: For a base below one, a logarithm is negative exactly when its argument exceeds one.
steps: The inequality is equivalent to (x²-2x)/(x-3)>8.
A sign chart at 3,4,6 gives positive intervals (3,4) and (6,∞).
The strict bound u>8 automatically ensures all logarithm arguments are positive.

problems.title: Volume cut off by a vertical midpoint plane
problems.question: A regular triangular pyramid has base side a and base dihedral angle 45°. A plane perpendicular to the base passes through the midpoints of two base sides. Find the cut-off corner pyramid’s volume.
problems.idea: The cut-off piece is a tetrahedron with one quarter of the original base area and three quarters of the original height.
formulas: Equilateral base area B=a²√3/4; inradius r=a√3/6.
steps: Let A be the common base vertex and E,F the two side midpoints. The triangle AEF has area B/4.
The base centre O lies two-thirds of the way from A to the opposite side; the vertical cutting plane is halfway along that same base altitude.
Therefore the intersection P of the cutting plane with the apex-to-A edge lies three-quarters of the way from A to the apex. Its height above the base is 3h/4.
The cut-off tetrahedron A-E-F-P has volume (1/3)(B/4)(3h/4)=Bh/16.
Substitute B,h: Bh=a³/8, so the cut-off volume is a³/128.

problems.title: Trapezoid-base pyramid with a given longest edge
problems.question: A pyramid has isosceles-trapezoid base with parallel sides 3,5 cm and legs 7 cm. Its height meets the diagonal intersection, and its longest lateral edge is 10 cm. Find its volume.
problems.idea: Find the farthest base vertex from the diagonal intersection.
formulas: Trapezoid diagonals divide each other in the ratio of the bases.
steps: The trapezoid altitude is √(49-1)=4√3 and area (3+5)·4√3/2=16√3.
A diagonal has horizontal projection (3+5)/2=4, so its length is √(16+48)=8.
The intersection divides it in ratio 5:3, giving vertex distances 5 and 3. The greatest is 5.
The pyramid height is √(10²-5²)=5√3.
Its volume is (1/3)(16√3)(5√3)=80 cm³.

problems.title: Triangular-frustum volume from its surface areas
problems.question: A regular triangular-pyramid frustum has base sides 30 m and 20 m. Its lateral area equals the sum of its base areas. Find its volume.
problems.idea: Find the slant height from area, then the vertical height by Pythagoras.
steps: The base areas are 225√3 and 100√3, with sum 325√3.
The perimeters are 90 and 60, so 75l=325√3 and l=13√3/3.
The inradius difference is (30-20)√3/6=5√3/3. Hence h=√(169/3-25/3)=4√3.
The geometric mean of the base areas is 150√3.
